title: Comparison of different loading protocols after intra-articular corticosteroid injection (IACSI) to the lower extremity in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) - A multicenter prospective registry of the Society for Pediatric and Adolescent Rheumatology (GKJR)
summary:
Due to the significantly differing post-treatment strategies of the various treatment centers and the lack of recommendations/guidelines, a study is needed to investigate this in more detail. 
The aim of this study is to set up a registry to compare treatment results based on different joint loads after injection with corticosteroids. This study will investigate whether different joint loads after an injection in the knee influence the time to reactivation of the disease or subsequent signs of inflammation, or whether there is a correlation between the load and the time to reactivation. The aim of this is to check whether it is necessary to relieve the strain or apply strain after an injection. Children and adolescents between the ages of 6 and 18 with a JIA diagnosis, gonarthritis and planned knee injections will be included in the study.
(The long-term goal of this and subsequent projects is to define weight-bearing parameters that influence the healing process after an IACSI in order to develop a consensus-based guideline for weight-bearing recommendations based on suitable parameters for IACSI of the lower extremity and to be able to make an individual weight-bearing recommendation).

interventions.name:
Each participating center pursues different post-treatment strategies. Two different stress groups were identified through survey results. Each center sticks to its own treatment procedure, which means that the group membership is determined by the centers' post-treatment strategies.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of JIA, oligo- or polyarthritis category according to ILAR criteria
- Therapeutic use of forearm crutches and/or therapy rollers possible 
- IACSI knee
- Consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Additional IACSI on other joints of the lower extremity (ankle/hip)
- Cortisone shock treatment within four weeks before/after the procedure
- Bony damage to the joint
- Surgery on the knee
- Lack of understanding
